concept.title: A thin lens image must be supported by independent principal rays
concept.inferential_jump: Several principal-ray rules are alternative constraints on one thin-lens ray bundle; any valid pair must locate the same image point.
entry_assumptions: Can trace refracted rays and identify real versus backward-extension intersections.

teaching_path.action: Draw the principal axis, optical centre O, and focal points F1 and F2 before tracing a spherical-lens image.
teaching_path.why_valid: Every principal ray rule is defined relative to this shared geometry.

teaching_path.action: For a convex or concave thin lens, apply two independent principal-ray rules consistently to the same object point.
teaching_path.why_valid: A valid image is a property of the whole refracted bundle; two independent constrained rays must agree on one image or backward-extension point.
teaching_path.output: object point -> two consistent principal rays -> image point

teaching_path.action: Use a distant-object convex-lens setup to connect nearly parallel incident rays with an image near the principal focus.
teaching_path.why_valid: A distant object supplies an approximate parallel bundle, which is the operational basis of the standard focal-length practical.
teaching_path.output: distant object -> near-parallel rays -> focal region check

predict.prompt: Why should a second principal ray be drawn if the first ray already looks as though it points to an image?
predict.defensible_answer: Because the image point is constrained by the whole ray bundle; an independent ray must agree on the same intersection.

attempt.produces: A labelled thin-lens diagram using two independent valid principal rays.

rubric.criterion: Principal axis, optical centre and focal points are labelled.
Two independent rays meet at one image or common backward-extension point.
rubric.evidence_of: Treating the image as a ray-bundle property rather than a memorized location.

accepted: Two valid principal rays agree on one physical or backward-extension image point.
rejected: One decorative ray is enough; the image is wherever that ray is drawn to go.

route.ask: Which geometric labels must every principal-ray rule share?
route.why_this_ask: It establishes the common lens geometry.

route.ask: What does a second independent ray contribute?
route.why_this_ask: It makes the image location a constrained result.

route.ask: What special incident bundle does a very distant object approximately provide?
route.why_this_ask: It links the geometry to the focal-length practical.

reconstruct.differs_from_teaching_path: The declarative route lists the principal-ray rules; the elicitation route starts from why multiple independent rays must agree before the finished diagram is trusted.

boundary_test.prompt: For a concave lens with a real object, do the outgoing rays physically meet on the far side of the lens?
boundary_test.answer: No. They diverge; their backward extensions meet on the object side to define a virtual image.
boundary_test.confirms: Real versus virtual is determined by physical ray intersection versus backward-extension intersection.

misconceptions.wrong_idea: Any ray through the optical centre of a thin lens must bend toward the focus.
misconceptions.diagnostic_prompt: In the Grade-10 thin-lens ray model, what happens to a ray directed through the optical centre?
misconceptions.repair: Use the thin-lens principal-ray rule: a ray through the optical centre is treated as undeviated in the simple paraxial construction.

exit_task.prompt: For a convex thin lens with an object outside the focal point, describe two independent principal rays you would use to locate the image and state what their common intersection tells you. Do not use the lens formula.

answer.summary: Use any two valid principal rays, such as parallel-to-axis then through the far focus, and through the optical centre approximately undeviated. Their physical intersection locates the real image point.
reasoning: Both rays start from the same object point.
Each obeys a different thin-lens principal-ray rule.
Agreement at one physical intersection independently determines the image.
answer.check: If two valid rays predict different image points, the construction or labels are inconsistent.

oracle.no_numeric_claim: The exit is a geometric construction/explanation and contains no computed numerical value.
